A73EGS-P.interesting_facts: Cataloged taxon in the 152-class deep learning marine classification benchmark.

Bangus.habitat: Coastal waters, estuaries, mangroves, and brackish lagoons
Bangus.geographic_distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to Hawaii and the Galápagos
Bangus.diet: Cyanobacteria, soft algae, small benthic invertebrates, and detritus
Bangus.typical_size: 50 - 100 cm (up to 180 cm, max weight ~14 kg)
Bangus.interesting_facts: National fish of the Philippines; capable of thriving in completely fresh water as well as hypersaline lagoons.

Big Head Carp.habitat: Large rivers, floodplain lakes, and calm reservoirs
Big Head Carp.geographic_distribution: Native to eastern Asia (China, Amur basin); widely introduced worldwide
Big Head Carp.diet: Filter feeder primarily consuming zooplankton and large phytoplankton
Big Head Carp.conservation_status: Data Deficient / Invasive in North America
Big Head Carp.interesting_facts: Possesses specialized gill rakers capable of straining microscopic zooplankton from turbid river currents.

Black Spotted Barb.habitat: Freshwater streams, rivers, and coastal marshes with heavy vegetation
Black Spotted Barb.geographic_distribution: Endemic to the Western Ghats and southwest coast of India
Black Spotted Barb.diet: Omnivore: aquatic insects, worms, algae, and botanical matter
Black Spotted Barb.interesting_facts: Adult breeding males display striking filamented dorsal fin rays and iridescent emerald-black blotches.

Catfish.habitat: Muddy freshwater rivers, swamps, ponds, and low-flow canals
Catfish.geographic_distribution: Global freshwater basins, prominent in Southeast Asia and the Americas
Catfish.diet: Carnivorous/Omnivorous bottom feeder: insects, crustaceans, mollusks, and small fish
Catfish.interesting_facts: Possesses sensitive barbels lined with olfactory receptors enabling navigation and hunting in zero-visibility waters.

Climbing Perch.habitat: Swamps, canals, lakes, and rice paddies
Climbing Perch.geographic_distribution: South and Southeast Asia: India to Indonesia and the Philippines
Climbing Perch.diet: Small fish, aquatic invertebrates, water plants, and detritus
Climbing Perch.interesting_facts: Equipped with a specialized labyrinth organ that allows breathing atmospheric oxygen and overland migration between dried ponds.

Fourfinger Threadfin.habitat: Coastal waters, sandy beaches, muddy bays, and estuaries
Fourfinger Threadfin.geographic_distribution: Indo-West Pacific: Persian Gulf to Australia and southern Japan
Fourfinger Threadfin.diet: Small pelagic crustaceans, polychaetes, and small schooling fish
Fourfinger Threadfin.interesting_facts: Possesses four distinct free sensory pectoral filaments used to probe turbid sea beds for buried prey.

Freshwater Eel.habitat: Estuaries, freshwater creeks, canals, and flooded wetlands
Freshwater Eel.geographic_distribution: Tropical Indo-Pacific and Southeast Asian inland waters
Freshwater Eel.diet: Crustaceans, aquatic insects, worms, and small fishes
Freshwater Eel.interesting_facts: Catadromous life cycle: migrates thousands of nautical miles into deep ocean trenches to spawn after maturing in rivers.

Glass Perchlet.habitat: Sluggish freshwater streams, ponds, estuaries, and rice fields
Glass Perchlet.geographic_distribution: South Asia: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Myanmar
Glass Perchlet.diet: Micro-crustaceans, mosquito larvae, and small benthic worms
Glass Perchlet.interesting_facts: Features an almost completely transparent body showing the spine, swim bladder, and internal viscera.

Goby.habitat: Tidal creeks, estuaries, coral reefs, and sandy river beds
Goby.geographic_distribution: Worldwide in temperate and tropical coastal zones
Goby.diet: Copepods, small amphipods, polychaetes, and algae
Goby.interesting_facts: Their pelvic fins are fused into a disc-shaped sucker that anchors them to rocks in surging tidal currents.

Gold Fish.habitat: Slow-moving freshwater rivers, quiet ponds, and ornamental aquaria
Gold Fish.geographic_distribution: Native to East Asia; domesticated and distributed globally
Gold Fish.diet: Plants, small crustaceans, detritus, and insect larvae
Gold Fish.interesting_facts: One of the earliest domesticated aquatic species, bred selectively in China for over a millennium.

Gourami.habitat: Swamps, marshlands, and weed-choked sluggish lowland rivers
Gourami.geographic_distribution: Southeast Asia: Mekong, Chao Phraya, and Indonesian archipelago
Gourami.diet: Aquatic vegetation, insects, algae, and small benthic fauna
Gourami.interesting_facts: Builds intricate buoyant bubble nests at the water surface where eggs are deposited and guarded by males.

Grass Carp.habitat: Large turbid rivers and connected floodplain lakes
Grass Carp.geographic_distribution: Native to East Asia (Amur to Pearl River); widely farmed internationally
Grass Carp.diet: Strictly herbivorous as adults: submerged macrophytes and emergent vegetation
Grass Carp.interesting_facts: Capable of consuming their own body weight in aquatic weeds daily; utilized globally for aquatic vegetation control.

Green Spotted Puffer.habitat: Mangroves, freshwater streams, and coastal brackish estuaries
Green Spotted Puffer.geographic_distribution: South and Southeast Asia: India, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Indonesia
Green Spotted Puffer.interesting_facts: Possesses beak-like dental plates to crush snail shells and synthesizes potent neurotoxins (tetrodotoxin) in its organs.

Indian Carp.habitat: Rivers, oxbow lakes, and aquaculture ponds of South Asia
Indian Carp.geographic_distribution: Northern and central India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, and Myanmar
Indian Carp.diet: Column feeder consuming plankton, filamentous algae, and decaying vegetal matter
Indian Carp.interesting_facts: One of the top cultured aquaculture species on earth, forming the cornerstone of South Asian inland polyculture.

Indo-Pacific Tarpon.habitat: Open marine waters, coastal bays, estuaries, and river mouths
Indo-Pacific Tarpon.geographic_distribution: Indo-Pacific: Red Sea and East Africa to French Polynesia
Indo-Pacific Tarpon.diet: Small schooling fish, shrimps, and crabs
Indo-Pacific Tarpon.interesting_facts: Possesses a lung-like vascularized swim bladder allowing it to swallow atmospheric air in hypoxic waters.

Jaguar Gapote.habitat: Turbid lakes, ponds, springs, and sluggish rivers with muddy bottoms
Jaguar Gapote.geographic_distribution: Central America: Atlantic slope from Honduras to Costa Rica
Jaguar Gapote.diet: Apex piscivore: small fishes and macro-invertebrates
Jaguar Gapote.interesting_facts: Exhibits extreme parental investment, aggressively protecting fry nests from all approaching predators.

Janitor Fish.habitat: Warm, slow-moving freshwater streams, canals, and eutrophic lakes
Janitor Fish.geographic_distribution: Native to the Amazon basin; invasive across tropical Asia and North America
Janitor Fish.diet: Benthic periphyton, algae, detritus, and aquatic biofilms
Janitor Fish.interesting_facts: Equipped with heavy dermal bone scutes resembling plate armor and burrows deep into river banks, accelerating erosion.

Knifefish.habitat: Lakes, swamps, and calm river backwaters with submerged timber
Knifefish.geographic_distribution: Southeast Asia: Mekong and Chao Phraya river basins
Knifefish.diet: Nocturnal carnivore preying on fishes, shrimp, and crustaceans
Knifefish.interesting_facts: Undulates a continuous elongated anal fin enabling precise forward and reverse swimming without turning.

Long-Snouted Pipefish.habitat: Shallow coastal eelgrass meadows and estuarine macroalgae beds
Long-Snouted Pipefish.geographic_distribution: Eastern Atlantic, Mediterranean, and Black Sea
Long-Snouted Pipefish.diet: Small mysid shrimp, amphipods, and larval fishes
Long-Snouted Pipefish.interesting_facts: Exhibits sex-role reversal: females compete for mates while males incubate fertilized eggs in an abdominal pouch.

Mosquito Fish.habitat: Shallow, vegetated ponds, ditches, drainage canals, and sluggish bayous
Mosquito Fish.geographic_distribution: Native to eastern North America; introduced globally for vector control
Mosquito Fish.interesting_facts: Gives birth to live young (viviparous) and tolerates extreme temperatures and high water salinity.

Mudfish.habitat: Lowland swamps, vegetated oxbows, and sluggish backwaters
Mudfish.geographic_distribution: Eastern North America: St. Lawrence River to the Gulf Coast
Mudfish.diet: Ambush predator: fish, crawfish, frogs, and mollusks
Mudfish.interesting_facts: Sole surviving species of the archaic order Amiiformes, dating back to the Jurassic period.

Mullet.habitat: Coastal waters, estuaries, harbors, lagoons, and freshwater rivers
Mullet.geographic_distribution: Worldwide in coastal temperate and tropical oceans
Mullet.diet: Detritus, microalgae, benthic diatoms, and sediment organic matter
Mullet.interesting_facts: Frequently leaps completely out of the water; possesses a muscular gizzard-like stomach to grind inorganic sediment.

Pangasius.habitat: Deep pools and turbid channels of large tropical river systems
Pangasius.geographic_distribution: Southeast Asia: Mekong and Chao Phraya basins
Pangasius.diet: Omnivore: crustaceans, algae, macroinvertebrates, and organic debris
Pangasius.conservation_status: Endangered in native wild basins / Extensively farmed
Pangasius.interesting_facts: Performs long seasonal upstream migrations to spawn during the onset of the Southeast Asian monsoon flood season.

Perch.habitat: Clear freshwater lakes, slow rivers, and brackish Baltic inlets
Perch.geographic_distribution: Eurasia: from Britain across northern Asia to eastern Siberia
Perch.diet: Piscivorous hunter: small fish, aquatic insects, and crayfish
Perch.interesting_facts: Distinctive dark vertical tiger stripes camouflage the fish among reeds and submerged vegetation.

Scat Fish.habitat: Coastal mangrove creeks, muddy estuaries, and lower river reaches
Scat Fish.geographic_distribution: Indo-Pacific: India to Japan, the Philippines, and northern Australia
Scat Fish.diet: Filamentous algae, detritus, small invertebrates, and macroalgae
Scat Fish.interesting_facts: Juveniles inhabit pure freshwater streams and migrate downstream into hypersaline reef shallows upon maturity.

Silver Barb.habitat: Rivers, streams, reservoirs, and inundated floodplains
Silver Barb.geographic_distribution: Mekong and Chao Phraya basins, Malay Peninsula, Sumatra, Java
Silver Barb.diet: Aquatic macrophytes, terrestrial plants falling into water, and filamentous algae
Silver Barb.interesting_facts: Key food fish across Indochina, valued for weed clearance in irrigation networks and polyculture ponds.

Silver Carp.habitat: Major rivers, canals, and connected floodplains with moderate current
Silver Carp.geographic_distribution: Native to East Asia; globally invasive in temperate river systems
Silver Carp.diet: Specialized filter feeder consuming microscopic phytoplankton
Silver Carp.conservation_status: Near Threatened in native range / Invasive in North America
Silver Carp.interesting_facts: Noted for sensational leaping behavior, propelling themselves up to 3 meters above the water when startled by motorboats.

Silver Perch.habitat: Turbid lowland rivers, billabongs, and drainage impoundments
Silver Perch.geographic_distribution: Murray-Darling river basin in southeastern Australia
Silver Perch.diet: Aquatic insects, algae, small mollusks, and zooplankton
Silver Perch.conservation_status: Critically Endangered in wild natural rivers (IUCN)
Silver Perch.interesting_facts: Wild populations plummeted dramatically due to river regulation and flow alterations, rescued through captive conservation programs.

Snakehead.habitat: Stagnant rivers, swamps, paddy fields, and weed-choked wetlands
Snakehead.geographic_distribution: Southern Asia, China, and Southeast Asia
Snakehead.diet: Voracious ambush predator: fishes, frogs, water snakes, and rodents
Snakehead.interesting_facts: Breathes atmospheric air via suprabranchial organs and can survive encased in wet mud during prolonged droughts.

Tenpounder.habitat: Shallow coastal waters, barrier lagoons, and mangrove bays
Tenpounder.diet: Small schooling fish and decapod crustaceans
Tenpounder.interesting_facts: Passes through an elongated, transparent leptocephalus larval phase resembling eel larvae before metamorphosis.

Tilapia.habitat: Rivers, lakes, sewage canals, and warm tropical reservoirs
Tilapia.geographic_distribution: Native to central/eastern Africa; cultured worldwide in tropical aquaculture
Tilapia.diet: Omnivore: phytoplankton, periphyton, floating macrophytes, and benthic detritus
Tilapia.interesting_facts: Maternal mouthbrooder: female holds eggs and newly hatched sac-fry inside her buccal cavity until they swim freely.
